text:
inc-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: p99 latency breach on canary rollout: encoder-service v8. Canary shard id=canary-3. Thresholds: p95>300ms, p99>800ms. Current p99 ~2.1s. Streaming stall >5s observed. Paging maya (oncall).

maya (oncall): seeing the alert, grabbing logs. which customers on canary-3?

inc-bot: affected routes: /v1/generate-stream, /v1/tokenize-stream. Downstream customers: glassbox-enterprise (10% traffic to canary), internal-eval (shadowing).

maya (oncall): @sophie can you pull encoder pod metrics and recent deploy history for canary-3? I want to know if this correlates to the v8 encoder rollout.

sophie (runtime): pulling metrics now. p95 jumped from ~260ms -> 480ms at 1953099960, p99 spiked to 2.1s at 1953099980. Pod CPU on canary-3 pods at ~85%, GPU mem stable. Notable: kernel queue length increased and streaming send latency increased sharply.

radek (ml): v8 encoder introduced an alternate attention kernel and a streaming buffer change (adaptive chunking). Could be head-of-line when batching + adaptive chunks mix.

maya (oncall): can we repro locally with a small workload? if batching + adaptive chunking combo causes stalls we might need to flip the flag back for canary.

liam (sre): paging in case we need routing changes. Suggest immediate mitigation: 1) route traffic off canary-3 for user-facing routes 2) set encoder adaptive_chunking=false for canary 3) if rollback needed, trigger rollback to v7. Which is faster?

maya (oncall): ordering: route first (no deploy risk), then toggle flag on canary, then rollback if still bad. evan (deploy-bot) can we shadow route away?

evan (deploy-bot): routing update planned: shift 80% of canary-3 traffic back to stable pool over 2m using weighted routing. Command queued.

(evans's command output)

```
# evan: routing update
route:update --from canary-3 --to stable-pool --weight 80 --duration 120s
Status: accepted, started at 1953100020
```

maya (oncall): applying adaptive_chunking=false on canary-3 now (runtime feature flag). Sophie pls confirm rollout of flag.

sophie (runtime): feature-flag flip issued to canary-3: `encoder.adaptive_chunking=false`. Propagating.

(quick traceback/log snippet)

```
2026-03-14T10:00:12Z canary-3 encoder[pid=2345]: stream_writer stalled for 5200ms waiting on chunk/kv-cache
2026-03-14T10:00:14Z canary-3 encoder[pid=2345]: batching window flushed late (200ms)
```

radek (ml): that stash behavior matches head-of-line blocking from variable chunk sizes combined with continuous batching. Good call flipping the flag.

maya (oncall): monitoring. p99 down to ~1.1s after routing shift and flag flip but still above SLO. Any sign of full recovery?

liam (sre): p99 trending down. Current p95=370ms p99=1.05s. Streaming stall counts dropped 70% in last 90s. Recommend scale up encoder pool for canary nodes by +1 instance to smooth KV-cache eviction.

evan (deploy-bot): scaling encoder pool +1 for canary-3. Command: `infra scale encoder canary-3 +1`

```
Status: scaled, new pod canary-3-7 in provisioning
```

maya (oncall): julie (cs) please prepare a short note for glassbox: they saw elevated latency for a subset of their requests for ~4 minutes; we are mitigating now and will follow up with root cause.

julie (cs): on it. sending immediate ack to glassbox and offering status. Will include postmortem once triage complete.

maya (oncall): ok current status: routing shifted, feature flag flipped, scaled pool. p99 now ~720ms, p95=330ms. Still borderline but under the SLO threshold of 800ms for p99. Streaming stalls near zero.

radek (ml): capture a run of failing traces before we flip flag or rollback. we have a few traces showing large chunk sizes + long batch coagulation. will upload examples to the incident doc.

liam (sre): recommend keeping canary-3 at 20% traffic for another 15m and monitor. if any regression reappears revert routing and roll back v8. We should also add an automatic fallback rule for future canaries: if p99 > 1.5s for 3m then auto-shift 100% to stable.

maya (oncall): agreed. I'll add the follow-up tasks. Handoff in 10m to liam. liam can you take lead for postmortem and rollout policy update?

liam (sre): taking handoff. Will own postmortem, create runbook entry for adaptive_chunking interactions with continuous batching, and implement auto-rollback policy.

julie (cs): Glassbox update sent: "We've observed a short-lived latency spike affecting a portion of your traffic during a canary rollout. Mitigations are in place and we will follow up with a detailed postmortem."

maya (oncall): summary for handoff to @liam:
- root alert: p99 spike ~2.1s on canary-3 after v8 encoder rollout
- immediate mitigations: weighted routing shift (80% off canary), feature flag adaptive_chunking=false, scaled encoder pool +1
- impact: ~4m elevated latency window, primary customer impacted glassbox-enterprise (~10% of their requests, ~12% of canary traffic), no data loss, streaming stalls resolved
- next steps: liam to own postmortem and policy changes, radek to supply failing traces, sophie to add gating test for adaptive_chunking + batching combo in canary harness

liam (sre): got it. I'll open the incident ticket and schedule a 30m postmortem. tagging: @radek @sophie for follow-ups.

maya (oncall): handing off oncall to liam at 1953100600. I remain available if needed. :thumbsup:

inc-bot: Incident mitigated: p99 < SLO for last 3m. Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident ID: INC-2026-1953100000

liam (sre): creating follow-up tasks now. thanks team.

(End of thread)
